title: Multi-Region Copy Trading: Ordered, Safe Fan-out
summary: Durably accept ordered lead events, then fan them out to many follower accounts.
Use per-lane idempotency, leases, and broker reconciliation for safe at-least-once processing.
Fail over with one execution owner while keeping accepted events replayable and auditable.

sections.title: Scale, Guarantees & Failure Boundaries
points: Handle 10,000 lead events per second, with one lead reaching 100,000 followers.
Preserve order per lead, while processing different leads in parallel.
Accepted events survive regional failure and show current follower trade status.
Safe recovery needs broker idempotency or a reliable result lookup.
speakingNotes: I would first define the guarantee and the main limit.
The platform accepts an event only after durable cross-region storage.
Every lead event receives one monotonic sequence number.
Different leads can run in parallel, but one lead keeps order.
Workers may receive duplicate messages after crashes or retries.
A broker needs idempotency or reliable lookup to avoid duplicate trades.

sections.title: Ordered Ledgers, Async Fan-out, Isolated Brokers
points: Assign each lead a home region and one ordered event ledger.
Commit the event and outbox record before returning success.
Fan out followers in chunks, then run independent ordered lanes.
Apply broker quotas and backpressure outside the acceptance path.
speakingNotes: I would separate fast acceptance from slow broker execution.
A home region assigns the sequence and owns normal processing.
A transactional outbox saves the event and publish request together.
A quorum commit completes before the API reports success.
The append-only ledger supports audit history and later replay.
Fan-out pages through large follower lists instead of one huge transaction.
Broker adapters hide different APIs and enforce per-broker capacity.

sections.title: Core Flow: From Lead Event to Follower Trade
points: Partition Kafka by leadId; the sequence number defines the event order.
Create unique, queryable intents for each event, follower, and action version.
Advance a lead–follower lane only after a terminal result.
Send a deterministic client order ID through every broker retry.
Read status from intents and reconcile uncertain provider results.
speakingNotes: The event ledger is the source for replay and audit.
Kafka preserves order for each lead, not one global stream.
Fan-out snapshots active subscriptions at the event sequence.
It writes intents with a unique event and follower key.
The intent state can be pending, executed, rejected, unknown, or skipped.
The lane pointer blocks the next event until this one finishes.
This protects order when fan-out batches finish at different times.
The adapter sends the same client ID on every retry.
The status page reads durable intents, so users see current progress.

sections.title: Production Safety: Crashes, Uncertainty & Failover
points: Crash and redelivery tests must prove one business trade, not one message.
On timeout, query broker state first; unresolved work stays UNKNOWN.
Unsubscribe writes a sequence fence; later work skips before broker submission.
Failover grants one region a fencing epoch and drains ambiguous lanes.
Replay repairs missing intents; alerts expose lag, drift, and broker failures.
speakingNotes: A worker crash after sending can leave the provider result unknown.
The worker checks broker history by the deterministic client ID.
If supported, it retries with the same ID; otherwise it stays UNKNOWN.
An unsubscribe records a clear cutover sequence number.
Existing in-flight calls may finish, but later events are skipped.
Failover waits for the old lease, then writes a higher epoch.
Old workers cannot update fenced state after losing ownership.
The same client ID protects against a late call at capable brokers.
Replay recreates missing intents from immutable lead events.
Alerts show queue lag, unknown age, broker errors, lease churn, and replication lag.

sections.title: Recommendation: Durable, Ordered, Honest Exactly-Once
points: Use durable acceptance, ordered per-lead events, and parallel follower execution.
Trade immediate confirmation for recoverability, backpressure, and clear eventual status.
Require broker idempotency or lookup; otherwise stop safely at UNKNOWN.
speakingNotes: My recommendation is asynchronous execution after durable acceptance.
Ordering stays local to each lead, while follower work scales out.
The trade-off is eventual status and more reconciliation work.
As volume grows, add fan-out shards and broker-specific capacity pools.
